text: {"findings":[{"rule_id":"MF-005","evidence":[{"kind":"title_block","ref":"heat_treatment","page":1,"quote":"--"},{"kind":"note","ref":"N3","page":1,"quote":"HEAT TREATMENT NOTE:- 1) PROFILE CUTTING SHOULD BE DONE. 2) TO BE CASE CARBURISING DONE. 2) TO BE INDUCTION HARDENED UPTO 50 ~ 55 HRC. 3) CASE DEPTH 0.8~ 1.2 mm."}],"comment":"The title block heat treatment field is '--' while note N3 specifies case carburising and induction hardening, but neither states the manufacturing stage at which each treatment applies (e.g., before or after final machining). The designer should fill in the heat treatment field and add the sequence of operations so the shop knows when to apply each treatment.","recommended_correction":"Update the heat treatment field and revise note N3 to state the order of operations relative to machining stages."},{"rule_id":"WPS-004","evidence":[{"kind":"dimension","ref":"D4","page":1,"quote":"⌀ 6 H7 (+0.012/0)"},{"kind":"dimension","ref":"D5","page":1,"quote":"⌀ 14 H7 (+0.018/0)"},{"kind":"title_block","ref":"surface_treatment","page":1,"quote":"I.Z.B.P. (TRIVALENT)"}],"comment":"Holes D4 and D5 carry tight H7 fits on a part that receives zinc plating per the title block, yet no allowance is made for the plating thickness on these mating diameters. Plating buildup will reduce the bore sizes and cause interference with mating pins or shafts. The designer should either specify masking of these holes during plating or adjust the pre-plate tolerances to account for the coating thickness.","recommended_correction":"Add a note to mask the H7 holes during plating, or open the pre-plate hole tolerances by the expected plating thickness."}]}
